newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's economy grows 6.8 pct in 1996 - Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile's economy grows 6.8 pct in 1996 - Aninat.

text.p: Chile's economy expanded 6.8 percent this year with consumer prices rising by around 6.5 percent, said Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
"We have completed a golden three years, shown by the harmony of all the indicators," Aninat told reporters.
"Growth is solid and around 6.8 percent...Inflation continues to fall and this year will meet our target of some 6.5 percent."
The figures showed the Central Bank's tight credit policy, which has been in force for over a year, has succeeded in slowing the economy, which expanded by a galloping 8.5 percent in 1995.
Chile's steady economic growth in recent years has doubled the country's gross domestic product over the last 10 years, to $86 billion in 1995, Aninat said.
Inflation -- falling for the sixth year in a row -- dropped from 8.2 percent last year.
Unemployment fell this year to 6.8 percent from 7.3 percent in 1995, said Aninat.
The economy's growth created 74,000 new jobs this year compared with 59,000 in 1995, he said.
